question: Based on current vault evidence, what are the strongest opportunities for Vector Network Analyzer in Wireless Communication, and what evidence supports each opportunity?
answer: The Vault has no page that ranks Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) opportunities in wireless communication, so these opportunities are pieced together from scattered mentions. The best-supported one is checking beamforming parts and accuracy for mobile network infrastructure. The MWC 2025 material pairs this with the R&S ZNBT multiport network analyzer (up to 40 GHz), which measures up to 24 ports at once in one instrument. A second opportunity is satellite and LEO user terminals. The Starlink user terminal test flow lists R&S ZNA for array calibration, next to Keysight PNA-X. The Kuiper user terminal test flow names a VNA as core equipment along with an anechoic chamber and a signal analyzer. A third opportunity is regulatory and SAR test labs for wireless devices. In these sources, a VNA and a vector signal generator help calibrate the SAR test system, and network analyzers are listed among the main instruments of wireless regulatory test labs. In every case the evidence only lists the products. None of it gives configurations, calibration methods, deal sizes or market data.
missing: No market sizing, revenue, deal or competitive data specific to VNAs in wireless; no ranking of opportunities; no VNA configurations, options or calibration procedures for the beamforming, Starlink/Kuiper or SAR uses.
